A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same entropic scheduling work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be reliably matched across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations on discrete distributions and Gaussian mixtures, plus ImageNet-64 generation results in Table 1 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds evaluations on CIFAR10, FFHQ and ImageNet-512, including spectral scheduling results and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The original entropic and rescaled schedules remain, but v3 introduces a spectral rescaled scheduler for pixel-space diffusion. Section 5.4 normalizes entropy separately in Fourier directions and weights their contributions by estimated amplitudes; Algorithm 2 supplies spectral error estimation. This adds a substantive scheduling component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates toy distributions and ImageNet-64. v3 retains these and adds CIFAR10 at 32×32, FFHQ at 64×64 and ImageNet-512, substantially broadening image populations and generation resolutions.

E2.justification: The retained ImageNet-64 comparison adds the spectral rescaled variant alongside EDM and rescaled entropy in v3 Table 4. Section 6.2 also explicitly compares against Karras et al.'s published Heun FD-DINOv2 score of 103.39; this is a cited reference result, not a documented rerun.

E3.justification: Added evaluations use unconditional VP EDM models and ImageNet-512 EDM2-XS/XXL checkpoints optimized separately for FID and DINO. Figure 4 adds a controlled qualitative comparison including NFE=8. The established DDIM budgets of 16/32/64, 50,000-image evaluation and retained ImageNet-64 settings remain unchanged, making this chiefly a configuration and control extension.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands diagnostic coverage with frequency-resolved entropy curves, matched-seed comparisons across sampling budgets, a 128-versus-512-point entropy-estimation check, and tests revealing worse performance with second-order solvers. Appendix H.3 also examines disagreement between FID and DINO across checkpoint types. The grid-sensitivity and higher-order findings are reported qualitatively.

E5.justification: Appendix H.3 newly specifies that image scores come from a single first run, and Figure 4 specifies matched random seeds. The toy experiments retain their 100 repeated KL estimates and uncertainty displays. No image confidence intervals or significance tests are added; the disclosure does not establish a change in run counts.

E6.justification: All 48 original ImageNet-64 scores remain unchanged in v3 Table 4, which adds spectral results. New datasets contribute substantial additional outcomes: for example, FFHQ stochastic DDIM at NFE=16 reports FID 40.48 for EDM, 30.81 for rescaled entropy and 30.61 for spectral rescaling. v3 also reports mixed deterministic spectral results, lower image brightness and second-order solver degradation.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Theorem C.1 and a proof connecting deterministic DDIM's Gaussian optimal schedule to the previously cited Euler result. Section 5.4 extends invariance reasoning to frequency contributions. The original entropy-rate, time-invariance, Gaussian rescaling and Tweedie derivations are retained, making this a limited theoretical extension.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, preserving the central invariance, loss-based estimation and sampling-improvement claims. The revised conclusion adds the spectral extension and an explicitly unproved conjecture about optimal scheduling for discrete tasks, while qualifying applicability to higher-order solvers.

C2.justification: v3 adds an important applicability boundary: observed benefits concern first-order solvers, with a tentative explanation involving second-order lookahead and information transfer. It also identifies spectral weighting as heuristic, leaves anisotropic and discrete optimality unresolved, and interprets FID–DINO disagreement. These substantially qualify v1's predominantly positive discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds scalar and FFT-based error-estimation pseudocode, an explicit cumulative integration procedure, 10,000-image amplitude estimation, and the smallest-model estimation policy. It also documents additional checkpoints and EDM implementation access. These materially expand reproduction instructions beyond v1's equations and Monte Carlo settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds dataset references for CIFAR10, FFHQ and ImageNet, plus Stein et al. on evaluation metrics. The related-work positioning against Dieleman, Li and other scheduling research is largely retained. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction, background and theoretical prose is retained. Changes include localized language corrections, author/header edits, new method and limitations subsections, reorganized appendices, and a rewritten conclusion emphasizing future work. The established narrative order remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v1's main ImageNet-64 table becomes an expanded appendix table, while v3 adds dataset tables and separate checkpoint-specific metric tables. A frequency plot, matched-seed comparison and high-resolution image galleries are added; some original galleries are removed. The workshop layout is also replaced by a preprint template, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the paper through broader image validation, explicit reporting of higher-order solver failures, and more reproducible estimator descriptions. These address v1's narrow image evidence and incomplete applicability guidance. The DDIM proof and checkpoint-specific metric results further clarify support for the method. Single-run image scores and qualitative robustness checks still limit confidence, particularly in the small, mixed spectral gains.
